text:
sarah-support: Heads up — customer Alex from Acme says ~25 users now get 403 when they try to open project settings for project `acme-prod` after an IDP cleanup last night. Example affected user: mike@acme.com. They also tried CLI and got the same 403 when listing members. Screenshot and a sanitized curl in the ticket.

james-se: Thanks. Can you paste the exact project id and one example request/response (headers redacted). Also was this via SAML/Okta SCIM or a manual group edit?

sarah-support: Project id is `proj_prod_9d2`. They ran SCIM group purge in Okta (removed ~10 groups, renamed 3). Here's the sanitized repro they provided: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <user_jwt>" 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/projects/proj_prod_9d2/members'
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "user is not permitted to view project members"
}
```

miguel-eng: :eyes: That response looks like the user lost role bindings rather than a token-scope issue. Two quick asks: 1) can support grab the ID token claims (sub, email, groups) for an affected user (sanitized) and 2) the last SCIM sync job id/timestamp from Okta logs? If groups were renamed the mapping likely didn't backfill.

alex-acme: We renamed the groups to match a new naming convention and then did a bulk prune (to remove stale service accounts). We did not touch users individually. We can grab claims if you tell us where to snapshot them.

james-se: If you can open the browser console on the user and copy the auth token payload (or export claims from your IdP), that helps. For immediate unblock you can invite the user directly to the project with an admin token: 
```
POST /v1/projects/proj_prod_9d2/invite
{ "email": "mike@acme.com", "role": "project-admin" }
# Requires org-admin or project-admin token
```
That will restore access while we repair the mapping.

sarah-support: I added the invite workaround to the ticket and asked Alex to share a single sanitized ID token claims blob and the Okta SCIM sync id.

miguel-eng: I'll queue an authz backfill to check for renamed-group->role regressions and reapply role bindings where the SCIM mapping used a previous group name. If the customer renamed groups rather than re-linking them we need to match on group external id or email patterns. I'll also run a dry run first.

deploy-bot: authz-backfill job queued by miguel-eng: job id `authz-backfill-1716054321`. Estimated runtime ~5-10m for dry run.

alex-acme: Ok. We've exported the ID token claims for mike@acme.com and uploaded to the support ticket (redacted). Thanks for the invite workaround, that helps.

miguel-eng: Got the claims, thanks. Dry run shows ~22 orphaned role bindings that map to renamed Okta groups. I'll kick the fix and follow up in the ticket. ETA ~2h (we need to run during a quiet window). If you need faster recovery, continue using invite route or we can run a manual one-off backfill for the 5 most-critical users.

james-se: Adding notes to the customer ticket with steps to avoid this in future: 1) preserve Okta group external ids when renaming, 2) run a SCIM sync in test mode first and review proposed deletions, 3) use our SCIM delta-report to preview membership changes.

sarah-support: Perfect — I'll keep the customer updated and mark this thread as linked to the ticket. Closing the Slack thread once migration fix is complete.

miguel-eng: Follow-up: fix applied, re-run complete. Confirmed access restored for the sample users. If Alex sees more 403s please reopen the ticket and include an affected user id and a trace_id.
